## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kukkujātaka* (Ja 396) is a birth-story included in the Pali Jātaka collection [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The narrative opens with the canonical verse beginning *Diyaddhakukku* ("The peak's a cubit"), reflecting the text's title [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at the Jetavana monastery in connection with an admonition given to a king (*rājovāda*), an introductory occasion noting that the full background story appears in the *Tesakuṇajātaka* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883].

In the story of the past, during the reign of King Brahmadatta in Benares, the Bodhisatta was born as the king's minister and counselor in worldly and spiritual affairs (*atthadhammānusāsako amacco*) [Fausböll 1883]. Having listened to the Bodhisatta's counsel, the king governed righteously, engaged in meritorious acts such as giving, and was reborn in the heavenly realm [Fausböll 1883]. Concluding the discourse, the Buddha identified the king of that lifetime as his disciple Ānanda and the wise minister as the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1883].

No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral or matched in DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In terms of Pali-internal text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 12 matching passages between the canonical text and the commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo), with the most extensive match spanning §6.1–7.4 of the verse text and §2897–2901 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
